obligations.source_text: Business rules found in app and step code move to step or actor configuration, with no default that encodes one flow: transcript.render's title format, Asia/Jerusalem time zone (transcript_render.py:118), right-to-left-unless-en rule, fallback word and texts, sections and CSS; llm.complete's cache name and label 'recording' (llm.py:171,174); repodocs' include folders (repodocs.py:197), spec-link and slug rules and culture.yaml project keys; library.push's filename rule, default format and author; attachment.fetch's accepted types (attachment_fetch.py:124); audio.transcribe's window plan; github.merge's merge method; decider's model and domain defaults; apps/github.py PR fact fields; the fixed Discord command reply text

obligations.behavior: a test fails when a flow name (fixer, pr-fix, newspaper, transcript, recording, devague) appears in culture_rules; it is green on the release branch
obligations.source_text: Generic modules name no flow: docstrings, examples and constants in library.py, email.py, llm.py, message.py, apps/github.py, apps/sonarcloud.py, apps/public_text.py, engine and node modules drop newspaper, transcript/recording, fixer and devague; a CI test fails when a flow name appears in culture_rules

obligations.seam: the live workflows of every enabled flow
obligations.behavior: after R3 each step of each live flow is a generic step or an app action (read from workflows show)
obligations.source_text: After the three releases: no module in culture_rules exists for one flow; every live flow (daily newspaper, Discord posts, recordings to the reader, repo docs, green-PR merge prompt, saves and sweeps) runs on generic steps and app actions whose choices are step or actor configuration; app code is integration surface only; the fixer's code, tests, bundle and live workflows are gone

obligations.seam: live runs and CI after R3
obligations.behavior: 3 scheduled newspapers and 3 days of recordings complete with 0 failed runs on generic steps; the flow-name test is green; a green-PR prompt merges on a click
obligations.source_text: A CI test finds 0 flow names (fixer, pr-fix, newspaper, transcript, recording, devague) in culture_rules; 0 built-ins named after a flow are registered; the next 3 scheduled daily newspapers and every recording in the 3 days after R3 complete on generic steps with 0 failed runs; the green-PR merge prompt still merges on a click

obligations.seam: live store via the release CLI (actors, variables)
obligations.behavior: after R1 the 4 fixer actors and 9 fixer-only variables are gone; checks_settle_min_s, checks_settle_timeout_s and ignored_check_apps remain
obligations.source_text: R1's live cleanup also covers the fixer's other live configuration: the agent actors claude-fixer, qwen-fixer, qwen-reviewer and codex-reviewer (disabled, then deleted) and the variables only fixer code reads (fixer_capacity_cooldown_s, fixer_comment_triggers, fixer_excluded_repos, fixer_levels, fixer_protected_paths, fixer_repos, fixer_stop_triggers, fixer_unavailable, trusted_authors); checks_settle_min_s, checks_settle_timeout_s and ignored_check_apps stay because node/checks_settle.py (the merge prompt's event) reads them

obligations.behavior: R1 drops no collection; the fixer's collections are still present after R1
obligations.source_text: R1 deletes no stored data automatically: the fixer's MongoDB collections (queues, handoffs, fixer_cooldowns, story_stops, fixer_status_comments, fixer_status_writers, reviews) are left in place after R1 and dropped later by an explicit admin step after a backup, so rolling R1 back is reinstalling the previous wheel and restoring the deleted workflows, rules and actors

obligations.behavior: the rollout pauses before the first upgrade and resumes after verify; fixer items are deleted, not purged, for at least a week
obligations.source_text: R1 rolls out paused (rollout pause, upgrade all 4 nodes and the API, verify, resume) so no node with the fixer code and none without it run side by side on live events; the deleted workflows and rules are deleted (restorable), never purged, until R1 has run a week

obligations.seam: live workflows of newspaper, recordings and repo docs (R3)
obligations.behavior: each is switched while the old built-ins are still registered, its saved previous revision applies by dry run, and the built-ins are removed only in a later build after the 3-run check
obligations.source_text: R3 switches each live flow before it deletes that flow's built-in: the switched workflow runs live (newspaper 3 scheduled issues, recordings 3 days, repo docs 3 cycles) while the old built-ins are still registered, so a rollback is one workflows update back to the saved revision; the built-ins are removed in a later build only after those checks pass

obligations.behavior: github.push and github.review_reply are not registered after R1
obligations.source_text: github.push and github.review_reply are removed with the PR fixer, since their only guard is the fixer's review record and chain lineage; they return behind a generic fence when a flow needs them (operator 2026-11-06, q5 a)

obligations.behavior: after R1 its params.actions lists only github.comment, its digest still matches the pin, and a green-PR prompt merges on a click
obligations.source_text: With github.push and github.review_reply removed (c24), the live github-app actor's params.actions drops them; the trust digest is unaffected (trusted.py:331-333 covers kind, machine, surface, commit_author, permissions and the connection, not actions), so the merge prompt keeps its pin. Narrowing the GitHub App's own Contents write permission and commit_author is a separate operator step that needs a new pinned digest

obligations.seam: core packages, the API and the web editor's action picker
obligations.behavior: no core module imports an app module or port (import test); the API serves the action catalogue from the registry and the picker offers a test extension's kind with no editor change
obligations.source_text: The core/extension boundary release (c19) also moves app-specific code that sits in core today into its app's side: GitHub's check settling (node/checks_settle.py) and webhook receivers (server/hooks/github.py, server/hooks/jira.py), the Discord gateway listener, and the web editor's hard-coded action catalogue (web/src/rules/ActionPicker.tsx:51-55, 'mirroring action_kinds.py'), which the API then serves from the registry so a new extension needs no editor change
